summary: Configured keepalived (VRRP) on node1 and node2 (OpenWrt 25.12.2, apk-installed) to share virtual IP 10.100.244.50/24 on br-lan, the private network they share with node3 (RHEL 7.9). node1 is MASTER (priority 150), node2 is BACKUP (priority 100), virtual_router_id 51. Demonstrated automatic failover: stopped keepalived on node1, node2 assumed the VIP within ~4s, and a continuous ping from node3 across the transition showed zero packet loss (icmp_seq 1-51 uninterrupted, only a transient ICMP redirect/latency blip, no drops). Restored node1 and the pair returned to its normal MASTER/BACKUP state (node1 preempts back due to higher priority). Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time (node1, then node2, then node3), each verified via a changed OS boot_id and post-restart proof: keepalived auto-started (enabled) and VRRP state/VIP placement recovered correctly on node1/node2, and node3 regained ping connectivity to the VIP after its own restart. Final state: node1 MASTER holding VIP, node2 clean BACKUP, node3 pinging VIP with 0% loss.
actions_performed: Inspected network topology and OS on node1, node2 (OpenWrt 25.12.2, br-lan 10.100.244.0/24), node3 (RHEL 7.9, eth0 same subnet)
Installed keepalived via apk on node1 and node2
Configured UCI keepalived: VIP 10.100.244.50/24 on br-lan, vrrp_instance VI_1, node1=MASTER priority 150, node2=BACKUP priority 100, virtual_router_id 51
Enabled and started keepalived on both nodes; verified node1 held VIP and node3 could ping it (baseline)
Started continuous ping from node3 to the VIP, stopped keepalived on node1 to force failover, confirmed node2 acquired the VIP and ping log showed zero packet loss across the transition
Restored node1's keepalived; confirmed it preempted back to MASTER and node2 returned to clean BACKUP; re-verified node3 connectivity
Captured baseline boot_id/uptime on all three nodes

Restarted node1 (adjusted reboot invocation since busybox lacks nohup), confirmed VIP failed over to node2 during the outage, node3 kept pinging successfully, then confirmed node1 came back with new boot_id, keepalived auto-started, and node1 reclaimed MASTER/VIP
Restarted node2 (VIP unaffected on node1 throughout), confirmed new boot_id and node2 recovered as clean BACKUP
Restarted node3 (used sudo /sbin/reboot since RHEL requires privilege escalation and full path), confirmed new boot_id, uptime reset, and restored ping connectivity to the VIP
Performed final full cluster health check: node1 MASTER with VIP, node2 BACKUP without VIP, node3 pinging VIP successfully

evidence.requirement: Shared VIP configured on node1/node2 private network, one node answers at a time
evidence.summary: UCI keepalived config committed on both nodes; after start, node1 (MASTER) holds 10.100.244.50 as secondary addr on br-lan while node2 (BACKUP) does not

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches the shared VIP under normal conditions
evidence.summary: node3 pings 10.100.244.50 successfully (0% loss) while node1 is MASTER

evidence.requirement: Automatic takeover by the other node when the first stops serving, demonstrated with node3 maintaining reachability across the transition
evidence.summary: Continuous ping started from node3; node1's keepalived stopped; node2 acquired the VIP within ~4s; ping log shows uninterrupted icmp_seq 1-51 (75 replies for 75 sent, 0% loss) across the failover

evidence.requirement: Pair restored to healthy redundant state after the demonstration
evidence.summary: node1 restarted keepalived, preempted back to MASTER with the VIP; node2 returned to clean BACKUP (no VIP); node3 ping to VIP succeeds

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node1 baseline boot identity and healthy state
evidence.summary: node1 boot_id 9f125e74-6b31-4452-be93-5b3840bedad1 captured before restart, VIP already confirmed held at this point

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out (node down); polling resumed with new boot_id 54d4a9ae-80fa-4032-9fb0-2bae0add3c72 and uptime 0 min; keepalived auto-started and node1 reclaimed VIP as MASTER; node2 confirmed released VIP; node3 ping to VIP succeeded during and after

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node2 baseline boot identity
evidence.summary: node2 boot_id eddc6d52-12a5-4d88-91c4-e071efe26969 captured before restart

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; connection timed out confirming outage; VIP verified still served by node1 (unaffected) during node2's restart; node2 came back with new boot_id 3ec4da99-0673-4b57-bb8f-7185078dc4d2, uptime 0 min, keepalived running as clean BACKUP without the VIP

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node3 baseline boot identity and healthy state
evidence.summary: node3 boot_id a8e7c48c-f025-4f14-9fd0-ef6c37642e45 captured before restart

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Confirmed sudo capability and reboot path on RHEL; reboot triggered via sudo /sbin/reboot; connection timeout then refused confirmed outage; node3 came back with new boot_id 3d4db582-dfd1-49b8-866d-247468b67819, uptime 0 min; post-restart ping from node3 to the VIP succeeded (0% loss)

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster health verification after all restarts
evidence.summary: node3 pings VIP successfully; node1 keepalived running and holding VIP as MASTER; node2 keepalived running as clean BACKUP without the VIP
